summary: Brandywine tower erected 1928 at 93 ft, rebuilt to 120 ft in 1938, moved to the Fairview Outdoor Education Center in Clear Spring; origin and height are disputed.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as standing with its cab no longer in place (Standing*)
facts.agency: Washington County Public Schools (runs the Fairview site where the tower now stands)

access.note: Part of a county school outdoor program; the sources read describe school use and no public visiting arrangement

events.note: Forest Worker report (1929, as quoted by Forest Lookouts): two steel observation towers erected in Maryland in 1928, one 93 ft high at Brandywine
Daily Times, Feb 15, 1938 (as quoted by Forest Lookouts): State Forestry Department announced rebuilding the 93-ft tower to 120 ft for two-way radio range
DNR draft report: moved from its original Brandywine location; now at the Fairview Outdoor Education Center, Clear Spring; property went to the University of Maryland; no date given
Washington County Public Schools sought bids for restoration work on the tower (steel structure, treads and landings, grounding); completion not confirmed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The state report places the Fairview tower at Brandywine (Prince George's County). The 2022 school article says it came from the Eastern Shore but cites no source, so the state record is followed and the article's claim is left unverified.

notes_for_editor: Height left unset on purpose: 93 ft (1928), 120 ft (1938 rebuild) and 104 ft (2022 school article) all appear. The DNR report is marked DRAFT and gives no move date. The Forest Lookouts page (cite 1) quotes the 1929 Forest Worker and 1938 Daily Times; both were read only as quoted there. Bay Journal 2022 article was not read (HTTP 429 twice). No staffing or fire records were found. Parent record data/towers/md/us-md-brandywine.json has agency set to 'March 1929:' (a stray date), and its height_m 28.3 is the 1928 93-ft height. Agency here means the current site operator, not the historical administrator.
